findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The kitchen’s sanitizer bucket was tested at 0ppm (quat). The sani solution was recreated and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer's recommended concentration to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: The gasket along the outdoor freezer is starting to tear. The PIC mentioned that new gaskets have been ordered to replace the current ones. Temperatures were observed compliant, however, be aware that the gasket will container to tear overtime. Ensure that gasket is replaced.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The women’s hand-sink is in need of recaulking. The current caulk is peeling away from the wall. Discussed with the owner and he mentioned that the facility will have the sink recaulked soon. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair to prevent accumulated debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: REPEAT- There were raw beef patties observed to be over milk, raw shelled eggs, jalapeños, and a container of dressing. This was discussed with the PIC and a handout on storage order was provided. CORRECTED- The raw beef patties were moved to be below these items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: There were reduced oxygen packages of salmon that were observed to be thawed and in the cooler. These packages of salmon state to remove from packaging prior to thawing and had not been removed from the packaging. This was discussed with the PIC who was informed that this fish either needs to be removed entirely from the packaging or a cut needs to be placed in the packaging prior to being thawed. CORRECTED- A cut was placed in each packaging of fish to correct the violation. Ensure that all reduced oxygen packaged fish is removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the kitchen, the triple sink in the kitchen, and the table next to the dish machine are all observed to need to be caulked to the wall. 
2. There are cracked gaskets on a cooler and a freezer in the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC who stated that they have ordered more gaskets and will be replacing them soon. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
REPEAT- The floors, walls, ceiling, and vent covers throughout the facility are in need of a deep cleaning. The walls, ceilings, and vent covers above the steam table, pizza oven, and the dish area were observed to have dust accumulation. The walls in the kitchen have built-up food splatter on them. Ensure that these physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned. 

The coolers/freezers and gaskets of them are in need of cleaning in the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC as well. Ensure that these are cleaned.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Several containers of shelled eggs were stored on the top shelf of a cooler along the cook-line. The shelled eggs were stored above Ready-to-eat food items such as but not limited to cooked rice. Discussed with PIC and eggs were placed on the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Be sure to always store raw animal protein below RTE foods to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Floors, walls, ceilings, and vent covers throughout the facility are in need of a deep cleaning. Vent covers and the ceiling above the steam table, pizza oven, as well as in the dish area, were observed with a significant amount of dust accumulation. The walls in the kitchen area were also observed with food splatter. When closing for the night or during slow periods, be sure to give the above described areas a deep cleaning and maintain as frequent as necessary.  

** The floor underneath shelves in the outdoor walk in freezer are in need of cleaning. Clean as frequent as necessary to prevent debris buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a container of burger patties to be stored above shrimp in a cooler. Discussed with PIC and containers were rearranged. Ensure that seafood is always stored above raw meats in order to prevent cross contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the ceilings and walls in the kitchen area to be soiled with debris. Ensure that ceilings and walls are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed turning off the faucet after hand washing without a barrier.  Discussed with employee, corrected on site.  Ensure faucets are turned off using a barrier to prevent recontamination.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed quaternary ammonium concentration in sanitizer buckets to be 75 ppm at the start of the inspection. The quat sanitizer container was recently changed and not primed. After refilling sani buckets the concentration was 300ppm. Sani buckets were remade during the inspection. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Pies in the front display cooler were observed to be 50F (probed).  Pies at the bottom of the cooler were 45F, the cooler was stocked at opening.  Inspector discussed not overloading the cooler to allow the cold air to be able to flow freely and evenly throughout the cooler.  Pies made with any milk-based items were moved to another cooler to bring the temperature back down to 41F.  Ensure the cooler is not over-stocked to prevent proper air flow and cooling.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 A tub of thawing fish with holes in the bottom allowing the running water to run out was observed. The fish on top was not fully submerged under cold running water. Kitchen manager placed fish in tub without holes. Best practices for thawing were discussed with kitchen manager.

TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple ceiling vents, tiles, and light fixtures throughout the kitchen that contained an accumulation of dust.  Keep these areas cleaned and dust free to prevent contamination.  Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly.

4-601.11: (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of re-caulking/sealing:
-along hand sink in kitchen
-above both 3 part sinks
-women’s restroom sink
-multiple holes in the NUDO board and walls throughout the entire kitchen and dish area.
Ensure these areas are caulked/sealed to create a smooth easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Flooring is peeling up and missing in multiple areas throughout the kitchen and dish area.  Floor coverings shall be smooth and easily cleanable.  Ensure floor is repaired to prevent food and soil accumulation.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Employee in dish area was observed rinsing hands at the sprayer sink by the dish machine. Employee stated they had soap in the dish area to wash hands at the sprayer sink before handling clean dishes. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was discussed. A few minutes later the employee was observed exiting the dish area with clean dishes and stated he washed his hands at the dump sink in the dish area when asked where handwashing occurred. Handwashing at the designated handwashing sink was once again discussed, and employee was advised to go around the corner and wash hands at the kitchen handwashing sink between handling dirty and cleaned dishes. Employee was later observed washing hands at the designated handwashing sink. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signs were not posted at the bar handwashing sink or in the men’s restroom. Handwashing signs were provided and posted.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Portobello mushrooms that were said to be rinsed prior to use were stored in original box in which they were received on the cook line. Proper storage in a clean, food grade container after rinsing was discussed. Clean food grade container was provided, and box was discarded. 
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee in kitchen was observed handling a personal bag while wearing gloves. Employee returned to the cook line and was about to prepare an order without changing gloves. Proper glove use and frequent handwashing were discussed. Ensure gloves are removed and discarded once they are potentially contaminated, including after touching personal items and general surfaces that are not considered clean.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Foods were observed with internal temperatures above 45F in the small cook line prep cooler located between the char-grill and fryers. Foods in the top of the prep cooler included Buffalo fish (46F), walleye (48F), catfish (52F), and frog legs (50F). Foods in the bottom of the cooler included shrimp (52F) and pork belly (51F). Shrimp and pork belly were moved from the 2 door reach-in cooler to the bottom of the prep cooler today and were moved back to the reach-in cooler. Products in the top holding compartment were said to have been refreshed around 2:30pm. Fish and frog legs were to be served or discarded by 6:30pm. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Small cook line prep cooler between char-grill and fryers was not maintaining foods at 41F/below during inspection. Cooler was observed at 50F with inspector’s stem thermometer placed in the bottom of the cooler with a hanging thermometer provided by manager during inspection. Foods that were not relocated to another cooler were to be used or discarded by 6:30pm (see #22 for details). Kitchen manger stated a call for service will be made for the cooler. Manager does not intend to use the cooler after today until the cooler is repaired and holding foods at 41F/below. Spot check will be conducted in 2 weeks to check on cooler function.
Equipment holding cold food shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain proper temperature of TCS foods.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Vacuum packaged Atlantic salmon was in various stages of thawing in the walk-in cooler. Proper thawing of reduced oxygen packaged fish was discussed. At minimum, packaging needs to be cut from the moment vacuum packaged fish is taken from the freezer to begin thawing in the walk-in cooler. If packages are thawed under running water, the fish much be removed from packaging as soon as thawing is completed. 
Reduced oxygen packaged fish that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in  (B) of this section.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.citation_text:
3-501.13 Tubs of thawing fish were stacked so a tub with holes in the bottom allowed for running water to fill the tub of fish below. Tub of fish on top had thawing product that was not fully submerged under cold running water. Kitchen manager placed fish in tub without holes and rearranged both tubs of fish to allow cold running water to flow over all surfaces of thawing fish via a split hose on the 3 part sink faucet. Best practices for thawing were discussed with kitchen manager.
TCS food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration at 41°F/below; (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F/below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Wiping cloths were observed in-use with spray bottles of sanitizer used for wiping tables. Proper storage of wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses versus single use paper towels with spray bottles were discussed. Rolls of paper towels were provided to use with spray bottles of sanitizer in the dining area. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 1) Floor, walls, attached plumbing and general surfaces underneath dish machine were soiled with buildup and debris in the dish area. 
2) Ceiling air exchange vent over cook line prep table had dust along the edges.
3) Buildup of food debris was observed along the walls at the corner of the cook line and under the 2 door cooler by the pizza prep cooler.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed quaternary ammonium concentration in sani buckets to be 0ppm at the start of the inspection. The quat dispenser was set to the hot water setting. After refilling sani buckets the concentration was 400ppm. Sani buckets were remade during the inspection. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the mop stored inside the mop bucket which does not allow it to air dry properly. Ensure the mop is stored in a position that allows it to air dry. The mop was hung during the inspection. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed an employee drink sitting on the pizza prep cooler. Ensure employee drinks are stored in a designated area or below food storage or prep surfaces. The drink was moved during the inspection. 
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the bar hand sink to have a cup and other items in it. The hand sink can only be used for hand washing only. Items may not be put inside the hand sink so it remains accessible for use. Items were moved out of the hand sink during the inspection. 
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on top of cutting boards and other parts of the cook line area. Wet wiping cloths must be put in a sanitizer solution between uses. 
(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed dust and soil accumulation on the shelves next to the pizza prep cooler. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned regularly and maintained clean. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
